attributes.residual:
STILL THE SAME SINGLE WEB, and it is now bracketed on FOUR sides rather than two. Ours: `bc: add r25,r31,r26 / c0: lwz r0,29216(r25)` ... call at 0x120 ... `13c: stfs f31,0(r25)`. Target: `b8: add r3,r31,r26 / bc: lwz r0,29216(r3)` ... `13c: stfsx f31,r31,r26`. Frame 96 vs 88, `lmw r25,52(r1)` vs `lmw r26,48(r1)`, seven callee-saved GPRs against six.

WHAT THIS PASS ADDS. (1) The web IS source-reachable -- axis D broke it outright -- but every form that breaks it does so by giving the address a SECOND SYMBOL ROOT, which costs 3 instructions against the 0 the web costs. The corrected statement of the cap is therefore not 'no lever exists' but 'no lever exists that breaks the web WITHOUT re-rooting the symbol', and that is a much narrower and more testable claim. (2) The prior record's entry-block finding ('nets to zero, pure intra-block scheduling, not what allocates r25') is INCOMPLETE: --ops shows the entry block carries a real insert/delete pair (ours has a surplus `addi r6,rX,0` where target writes `clrlwi r6,r28,24` directly, and target rematerialises `addi r4,r27,0` at BOTH ErrorPrintf sites where we hoist one copy into the entry block). Those balance at count level, which is why the prior pass read them as zero, but they are two distinct STRUCTURAL differences and axis S moved one of them. (3) Both remaining entry-block differences are address/copy PRE decisions of the same family as the r25 web, so the function has ONE mechanism at THREE sites, not one site.

DO NOT RE-PROBE: axis B (direct-global respelling), axis D (block-scoped local alias of the global -- same tax), axis E (single-use array-member view -- folds away), axis H (call-argument alias substitution), axis T / v1 A2 (inline (u8)type, now vetoed at TWO alignments), v1 A3 (delete wtarget), axis C (initializer moved LATER), axis Y (store-order swap).
